notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only tower-specific source is one row in the tnlandforms Georgia list (location, county, elevation, and a last field 'topo'). The list gives no unit for elevation; the story reads 738 as feet (about 225 m), which matches the 224.9 m in the record, and says so in the text. The 'topo' field is quoted as written and is not labelled a data source, because the list does not label it that way. No source read or searched gives a build date, builder, design, height, staffing, fire history, fate or access for this site, so the story has no built, staffing or fate sentences. Name collisions to avoid: Woodville, Texas (nhlr tx/woodville-fire-tower) and a Woodville lookout in Bertie County, North Carolina (cached FOREST LOOKOUTS page) are different towers. A federal antenna registry record for a structure of about 370 ft in Woodville, registered to Greene County in 2011, appeared in a search snippet only; it was not fetched or linked and may be a communications tower. The Flickr photo titled 'Woodville Fire Tower' (credit RandomConnections, via MAPLOGS) was not added to photos because its license and Flickr page were not checked. Verification pass 2026-10-21: removed 'small' (the population figure does not establish it); replaced 'data source' with 'last field'; flagged the missing elevation unit; reworded the statewide sentence so it no longer copies the Vanishing Georgia wording; added the 2020-census quote. The brief's county, coordinates and elevation match the list.
